key_insight: Ti3C2Tx MXene stability in perovskite precursor inks depends on the chemical constituents and their addition sequence: iodine species accelerate degradation, while methylammonium iodide provides surface passivation.
engineering_relevance: Controlling precursor composition and mixing order can help preserve and tune MXene surfaces during perovskite solar-cell fabrication.
method: Expose MXenes to individual and combined MAPbI3 precursor components.
Use X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy to characterize chemical and surface changes.
Apply density functional theory to investigate surface interactions.
evidence_signal: Combined XPS analysis and DFT calculations indicate rapid degradation with iodine and polyiodides, slower oxidation with PbI2, and hydrogen-bond-mediated stabilization with MAI.
watch_item: The abstract reports a model MAPbI3 precursor study, not quantified solar-cell performance gains; mixing order requires careful control.
paper_title: Dynamic Chemical Changes of Ti3C2Tx MXenes in Halide Perovskite Precursor Environments
